scope: Records the first Phase A slice of the disaggregated KV work: the KvBlockStore ABI, the block identity with epoch rules, the KvTierCoordinator state machine, and their host contract test. It does not touch the serving path, move any KV byte to a cold tier, compile CUDA, run a model, or measure performance.

checks.result: kv coordinator: OK; nine contract cases pass
1/1 test passed through the project's CMake target
aggregate_passed=true; the new kv-coordinator check is part of the gate; receipt build/reports/quality/receipt.json

findings: The imported v0.1.45 engine already implements the L0 and L1 tiers: a streamed QSA layer keeps its authoritative K/V in pinned device-mapped host memory, VRAM holds a bounded pool of page slots, and kv_stream_resolve makes the selected blocks resident with a CLOCK sweep on device. The coordinator therefore owns L1 admission, the store, and the epoch rules, and the device-side residency map stays the L0/L1 mechanism rather than something the coordinator reimplements.
The quarantined prototype's completion bitmap was indexed by the block inside its group, so two groups of the same layer shared a flag. The new coordinator indexes by the block itself.

A cold-read counter that only moves on success cannot prove a foreground cold read happened when the read is refused. The counter moves when the read is issued, and a separate failure counter records the refusals.
non_claims: No KV byte has moved between tiers; the store under test is an in-memory reference implementation.
The coordinator is not wired into verify.cpp yet: the serving append, selection, and resolve boundaries are unchanged.
No CUDA backend was compiled, no model was run, and no NLL, perplexity, throughput, or latency figure is claimed.
B550 was unreachable on both the LAN and ZeroTier paths for the whole session, so no hardware acceptance gate was run.
